page: Amazon Web Services c9g.4xlarge is a compute-optimized instance built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and powered by custom AWS ARMv9 Graviton processors using the Neoverse-V3 microarchitecture. It features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs operating at a clock speed of 3.3 GHz without hyperthreading. The server is equipped with 32.0 GB of memory, yielding 2.0 GB of RAM per vCPU, alongside 64 KB L1d, 2 MB L2, and 48 MB L3 cache configurations. Network performance is provisioned with a baseline bandwidth of 8 Gbps, while local disk storage is not bundled and no discrete GPU hardware is included.

In benchmark testing, the instance exhibits top-tier single-core performance, achieving high marks in single-threaded gzip compression, single-threaded bzip3 decompression, Geekbench single-core, and PassMark memory benchmarks. High memory bandwidth and rapid single-core execution also contribute to efficient small-model LLM text generation and text processing workloads. Multi-threaded operations, such as bzip3 decompression, Geekbench multi-core processing, PassMark database operations, and static web serving, demonstrate strong relative throughput within the upper quartile of benchmarked environments. Conversely, standard stress-ng execution, software compilation with Clang, ray tracing, and Redis SET operations record mid-range average scores.

The server offers dedicated hardware execution across all 16 physical cores on an ARM64 architecture, avoiding resource contention inherent to hyperthreaded virtual CPUs. The compute-optimized 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio provides a cost-efficient resource balance for CPU-heavy tasks without over-allocating memory capacity. However, reliance on network-attached EBS storage and the absence of integrated local NVMe SSDs or hardware accelerator GPUs restrict its utility for persistent direct-attached storage applications and large-scale parallel GPU matrix processing. The c9g.4xlarge is well suited for CPU-intensive tasks including static web serving, data compression pipeline execution, text processing, database operations, and lightweight CPU-based LLM text generation.
